decisions.context: Cameras operate along production lines, often without network access, so predictions must be available locally. The design space describes both on-device inference and offline containerized services.

alternatives.label: On-device edge inference
pros: Offline operation: inference runs on the device
cons: Tight budget: device rollout and support

alternatives.label: Containerized offline prediction service
pros: Offline operation: supports local batch prediction
cons: Local inference: service requires device-side runtime

decisions.rationale: Offline operation decides the choice: the model runs on the cameras even without network access, at the cost of managing model deployment across devices. This aligns with “Composing Deep-Learning Microservices for the Hybrid Internet of Things” and “Three Levels of ML Software.”
consequences: Package and distribute compatible model artifacts to cameras.
Device updates and recovery need to work when connectivity returns.

decisions.decision: How should weekly training and validation run?
decisions.context: The model is retrained weekly, which makes repeatable sequencing of training, evaluation, and release valuable to a small team. The design space contrasts manual script execution with an orchestrated pipeline.
decisions.rationale: The weekly cadence decides the choice: a repeatable pipeline reduces recurring manual work, though it adds workflow upkeep. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” support pipeline-based execution.
consequences: Define and maintain training, evaluation, and release stages.
Keep pipeline dependencies manageable for the small team.

decisions.context: Newly labelled images arrive for weekly retraining. The design space treats schedule-based retraining and data or performance triggers as practices that may be combined, rather than mutually exclusive alternatives.

alternatives.label: Schedule-based retraining trigger
cons: Label availability: may run without useful new labels

alternatives.label: Threshold-based retraining
pros: Label availability: can react to quality changes
cons: Small team: thresholds need tuning and oversight

decisions.rationale: The stated weekly cadence decides the choice: schedule retraining to match it and gate training on the availability of newly labelled images. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” describe recurring triggers; this gives up reacting immediately to drift between runs.
consequences: Skip or defer scheduled runs when new labels are unavailable.
Changes in image quality may remain undetected until the next run.

decisions.decision: How should candidate models be evaluated?
decisions.context: Weekly retraining creates frequent candidate models that need a consistent promotion check. The design space includes offline evaluation against held-out data and metric-driven candidate comparison.

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Safe weekly updates: checks candidates before deployment
cons: Small team: requires held-out data and evaluation upkeep

alternatives.label: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
pros: Small team: focused comparison on chosen metrics
cons: Safe weekly updates: metric choice can miss other regressions

alternatives.label: Threshold-based quality regression testing
pros: Safe weekly updates: blocks quality drops

decisions.rationale: Safe weekly updates decide the choice: evaluate candidates against held-out labelled data before promotion, accepting the work of maintaining that evaluation set. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” describe offline candidate validation and quality checks.
consequences: Preserve a held-out labelled set for comparison.
Set promotion criteria before automating device rollout.

decisions.decision: How should model releases be controlled?
decisions.context: A retrained model must reach devices that may be offline, so a failed release should not leave the production line without a usable model. The design space offers progressive release with rollback and unified release automation.

alternatives.label: Progressive release automation with rollback
pros: Safe weekly updates: incremental rollout and rollback
cons: Small team: rollout tracking adds operational work

alternatives.label: Unified release automation
pros: Small team: one automated build and release process
cons: Safe weekly updates: rollback behavior is not explicit

decisions.rationale: Safe weekly updates decide the choice: incremental rollout with rollback limits the impact of a bad model, at the cost of tracking release state across devices. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support this approach.
consequences: Retain the previous known-good model on each device.
Track which devices have received each model version.

decisions.decision: How much lifecycle state should be versioned?
decisions.context: Weekly training should be reproducible so the team can identify which labelled data and training configuration produced a deployed model. The design space ranges from artifact-only tracking to lifecycle-wide traceability.

alternatives.label: End-to-end reproducible lifecycle governance
pros: Reproducibility: links data, runs, artifacts, and deployment

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
cons: Reproducibility: omits training and dataset context

alternatives.label: Pipeline and experiment version control
pros: Reproducibility: records pipeline and experiment changes
cons: Safe weekly updates: deployment health is not included

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: link datasets, training runs, artifacts, and deployment status so weekly results can be traced, accepting added metadata work. “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It (from a Data Scientist Perspective)” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support lifecycle traceability.
consequences: Record dataset versions and training configuration for each candidate.
Keep traceability tooling and metadata proportional to the team’s capacity.

decisions.context: Devices may lack network access, while production images and predictions can change between weekly training runs. Monitoring and retraining triggers are represented as combinable practices in this low-exclusivity dimension.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
pros: Offline operation: drift summaries can be collected locally
cons: Small team: baselines and alerts need maintenance

alternatives.label: Service-health and data-quality monitoring
pros: Safe weekly updates: surfaces runtime and input problems
cons: Offline operation: centralized visibility is delayed

alternatives.label: Passive production operation
cons: Safe weekly updates: failures may stay unnoticed

decisions.rationale: Safe weekly updates decide the choice: observe input shifts between training runs, accepting the work of maintaining baselines. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Machine Learning Monitoring: What It Is, and What We Are Missing” support data and feature monitoring; collect summaries locally and synchronize when devices reconnect.
consequences: Buffer monitoring data locally during network outages.
Define a lightweight path to review drift and image quality changes.

uncovered: Device-to-device update transport and integrity when cameras are offline.
Model format, hardware compatibility, and device rollback mechanics.
Image retention, privacy, and newly labelled data transfer from production lines.
Latency, memory, and throughput targets for inference on camera hardware.
The specific defect-quality metric and acceptance thresholds for promotion.
